mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an imminent monetary easing, which reduces the discount rate for equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior month, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.0% in a monthly reading, it signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 55% of months where UNRATE drops below 4.0%, or average return in triggered months is not significantly positive (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate robust consumer demand, which accelerates corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or interaction effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During supply contraction phases (INDPRO < 95.0), industrial output declines intensify input costs and reduce corporate margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO < 95.0, or average return is not significantly negative (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI inflation exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation prompting Fed tightening, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 55% of months where CPIAUCSL yoy > 3.0%, or average return is not significantly negative (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months indicates strong labor market growth supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS has increased for three consecutive months, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions (GDPC1 growth > 2.5% annualized), rising housing starts (HOUST) signal overheating demand, triggering anticipated policy tightening that causes negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where HOUST rises and GDPC1 growth > 2.5% annualized, or average return is not significantly negative (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicate stagflationary pressures that erode corporate margins, driving negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining INDPRO and rising CPIAUCSL fails to produce negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or interaction effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05).
